closes.key: role-contradiction|Payment|GET /v1/payments/:reference: public and staff-only
closes.detail: GET /v1/payments/:reference: public and staff-only

decisions.decision: A5: GET /v1/payments/:reference is the payer's own (user:owner); staff read GET /v1/admin/payments/:reference; nothing about a payment is public.
A6: An audit row's actor is a staff id (name joined on read); every staff action writes one, in the same transaction as the change.
A7: The server decides which actions a wish, person, payment or order offers (the response carries actions); it masks phone and email for staff (the full value only with a reason, audited).
A8: Staff sign-in: a code to an email that is already a staff member in Team; no self sign-up; staff refresh life 12 h (as declared). The code and verify routes are the only public /v1/admin routes.
A9: A maker sees only the Concierge orders given to them; owner and ops see all. Ops may read Prices; only owner and finance change them.

A10: A price change carries typed old and new values in kobo and takes effect as a new price-book version; the 40% and its end date live in the price book's Promotion, never a page constant. The payout threshold is a price-book setting (R14).

A11: A refund goes through the payments port and reads 'Refund started' until the provider's webhook confirms it; the ledger's provider side comes from a daily settlement job; differences are rows staff can see, never auto-corrected.

A12: Numbers' targets are a staff-set setting (none set: 'No target set'); thread counts are their own read (GET /v1/admin/support/counts); a reply really sends an email; an inbound email (the email provider's inbound webhook, signature checked: POST /v1/webhooks/email/inbound) opens or reopens a thread.

A13: Style use counts (previews, paid uses) are written by events from the app, never invented; a wish records the style it was made in (Wish.style). Automatic checks on a submitted style run in the page and are re-run by the reviewer's page; the server stores the result with who ran it.

A14: Every /v1/admin request that changes something carries reason (string, 4 or more characters), written to the audit row, including the declared ones that lacked it. Only the staff sign-in routes (code, verify, sign-out) take none; code and verify are public by nature (before sign-in), rate-limited.

decisions.decision: A18: Same field: ConciergeOrder.maker = makerId; Payout.creator = creatorId; Report.wish = wishId. Different: Report.decided is the decision taken (enum), Report.decidedAt is when.

A19: Built though no screen names them: GET /v1/admin/support/counts, POST /v1/webhooks/email/inbound (signature checked), a daily settlement job (internal), PUT /v1/admin/numbers/targets (owner, finance; reason), POST /v1/admin/people/:id/contact-reveal (reason; audited; returns the full phone and email once).

The registry is frozen at 105 resources, 233 endpoints (73 under /v1/admin), 7 waves, 0 open conflicts. The owner handed over (R4: 'Proceed with full build the backend'), so the freeze is the lead's call under the skill's autonomous mode; the summary is listed to the owner. From here registry.json is read-only: an agent that finds it wrong halts and reports; a change is a new ruling, a re-run of tools/pipeline/reconcile.py and a new lock.
